subject: Information Theory
title: Signal Detection Theory
description: A 60-second lesson on Signal Detection Theory.

hook.text: A doctor reads a blurry scan. Is that shadow a tumor or just noise? Signal detection theory frames the answer.

buildup.text: Detection is a decision: signal present or absent? Two errors lurk: false alarm and missed detection.

discovery.text: Setting the threshold trades off the two errors. Lower the bar and catch more signals—but also more false alarms.

twist.text: The ROC curve plots this tradeoff. A perfect detector reaches the top-left corner. Random guessing is the diagonal.

climax.text: This framework governs spam filters, radar, medical tests, and any system that must decide under uncertainty.

punchline.text: Detect more, but cry wolf more often. Choose your tradeoff.

quiz.question: What does the ROC curve show?
options: The tradeoff between detection rate and false alarms
